why: A flop with one listed bet size, one distinct raise size, and a raise cap that allows a raise but not a re-raise. The ranges are nonidentical: OOP keeps suited connectors and JJ+, IP keeps TT+ and fewer connectors, on a jack-high two-tone flop. This is not the historical identical QQ,JJ,TT,99 flop. Flop infosets are stored per turn and river runout, so this is the runout-scale workload.
study_inputs_note: Ranges are study inputs for this benchmark. They are not a solved preflop equilibrium.
memory_note: 4096 is the engine allocation budget (--memory-mib), not an operating-system limit and not process RSS. The street default is 1024 MiB. The higher budget is headroom for runout infosets. The street-config document also records that budget.
eval_interval_source: --accuracy 0.001 hardcodes eval_interval to 20. There is no flag to change that cadence.
betting_note: One shared bet size (0.5) is used on the flop, turn, and river, with an explicit raise size (0.75). max-raises 2 lets the facing player raise and then stops; the opening bet counts toward that cap. The tree is benchmarks/study/configs/flop_srp_one_size.txt. All-in is a separate action.
